Billy Gene Coker

Billy Gene Coker, 89, of Perryville, passed away peacefully in his home on August 11, surrounded by the life and love he built over nearly nine decades. 

Born in Conway, Billy was the son of Alvis Coker and Amy Gunter (née Heffington). He was preceded in death by his parents; brothers, Bobby Coker, James Mahan, Larry Mahan, and Sandy Coker; and sisters, Alva Dean Coker, Carolyn Nagel, and Linda Coker. 

Billy was the beloved partner of Debbie Tate for 36 years and a devoted father to Caryn Burge and her husband, Jason, and Danny Coker and his wife, Tonya. He was a proud grandfather to Sara Coker, Jenna Coker, Jayme Denker, and Kaila Collins, and a loving great-grandfather to Reed Collins. 

Billy loved his family deeply and found joy in the simple things in life. He was an avid outdoorsman who loved hunting and fishing, spending time with the people he loved, and, of course, tossing back a few “cold ones.” 

Those who knew Billy will remember the life he lived, the stories he shared, and the love he had for his family. After 89 years, he leaves behind a lifetime of memories that will continue to be told, laughed about, and cherished by those who loved him most. 

He will be deeply missed and forever loved.

Visitation will be 1:30 to 2:00 p.m. Friday, August 14 at Ashby Funeral Home with his Celebration of Life to begin at 2:00 p.m.

Yvonne Lynn Martin-Caple

Yvonne Lynn Martin-Caple, 63, of Benton, Arkansas, passed away August 11, 2026. She was born February 16, 1963, in Charleston, South Carolina, to Emory L. Martin, Sr. and Hazel (Hobby) Martin.

Yvonne worked for many years in food service at the Arkansas Health Center. She was an incredible baker, and those who knew her best were fortunate enough to enjoy the sweet treats she made with her special ingredient, love. Her family especially looked forward to her Neiman Marcus brownies, fudge, dirt cake, and no-bake cookies. Whatever she made, it was always better because it came from Yvonne’s kitchen.

Anyone who stepped inside Yvonne’s home quickly discovered another thing she loved—angels. Her family often gave them to her as gifts, and over the years, she collected enough to have them displayed throughout her home. Each one was special, and together they became a beautiful reflection of something that brought her great joy.

Yvonne also had a love for flowers and plants and enjoyed spending time outdoors. She liked camping, although her version of camping was definitely more “glamping”—and air conditioning was not optional! She appreciated the beauty of the outdoors while still enjoying the comforts of home.

Above all, Yvonne treasured her family. Holidays, birthdays, and family gatherings were some of her favorite times because they meant being surrounded by the people she loved. She found happiness in the simple things—something sweet from the kitchen, beautiful flowers, time outside, and a house filled with family.

Yvonne was preceded in death by her parents, Emory L. Martin, Sr. and Hazel (Hobby) Martin; brother, Gary L. Martin; and two nephews.

She leaves behind to cherish her memory her loving husband of 38 years, Dennis Caple; sons, Jeffery Caple and wife Rebekah, and Jody Caple; sisters, Debra Stephens and husband Kevin, and Teresa Witham and husband Lance; brothers, Emory L. Martin, Jr. and wife Diana, Richard Martin and wife Nicole, Michael Martin, Jason Martin and wife Naomi, and Timothy Martin and wife Missy; 28 nieces and nephews; numerous great-nieces and great-nephews; and many cousins, extended family members, and friends who loved Yvonne and will miss her always.

Visitation will be held from 5:00–7:00 PM, Monday, August 17, at Smith-Benton Funeral Home, 322 N. Market Street in Benton, Arkansas.

Funeral service, officiated by Bro. Kirby Caple, will be held at 2:00 PM, Tuesday, August 18, at Smith-Benton Funeral Home. Burial will follow at McPherson Cemetery in Sardis, with Roger Fagan, Josh Holmes, Blake Narramore, Lance Witham, Phillip Koch, and Charles Caple assisting as pallbearers.

Yvonne leaves behind more than the things she loved and the treats everyone looked forward to—she leaves behind a lifetime of memories made with the people who mattered most to her. Her family will remember her in every gathering, every blooming flower, every favorite dessert, and perhaps even every camping trip made just a little more comfortable with some good air conditioning.

Raymond Wendall Wilbanks

Raymond Wendall Wilbanks, age 65, of Benton passed away on Monday, August 10, 2026. He was born March 11, 1961 in DeQueen, Arkansas.

Wendall was a loving husband, father, grandfather, son, brother, and friend. Anyone who knew Wendall knew how much he loved spending time with his family. His greatest joy was being with his grandchildren and making memories with the people he loved. In his younger years, Wendall could often be found working on cars, a hobby he enjoyed throughout his life.

He is survived by his beloved wife, Jamie Wilbanks; his children, Mary McConihay (Travis), Kristin Griffin (Mark), Corey Skinner (Megan), and Wendall Wilbanks; and his grandchildren, Cole, Aubree, Kaydence, Anna, Hadley, and Joshua. He is also survived by his parents, Jo Ann and Robert Wilbanks; and his siblings, Ramona Weiss and Richard Wilbanks.

Wendall was preceded in death by his siblings, Rose Marie Wilbanks, Ronald Wayne Wilbanks, Robert Lynn Wilbanks, and Rhonda Jo Price.

Wendall will be deeply missed by his family and all who knew and loved him. His love for his family, his devotion to his grandchildren, and the memories he created with those around him will remain in their hearts forever.

Visitation will be held Friday, August 14, 2026, from 9:00 to 10:00 a.m. at Ashby Funeral Home in Benton, Arkansas. Funeral services will follow, with Pastor Mark Blakely officiating. Burial will follow the service at FairPlay Cemetery in Glen Rose, Arkansas.

Jeffery Alan Ramsey

After more than four decades of serving his state, protecting his community, and standing beside countless people in their time of need, Senior Corporal Jeffery Alan Ramsey’s watch ended on August 7, 2026.

Born October 28, 1960, in Benton, Arkansas, Jeff was the son of Bill and Sarah Ramsey. His career in law enforcement began with the Saline County Sheriff’s Office before he went on to serve 33½ years with the Arkansas State Police. Known by his call sign A81, Jeff wore the badge with pride and earned the respect of those who worked alongside him and those he served. After retiring from the State Police, he continued serving his community as Chief of Police in Haskell for a year and a half.

Jeff was a protector by nature and someone others knew they could count on. He took his responsibilities seriously and was a mentor to many young officers, teaching not only the job, but what it meant to be a good cop. Beneath his strong presence was a generous heart, a sense of humor, fierce loyalty, and a genuine concern for others. His brothers in blue became an important part of his life, and the friendships he formed through his years of service remained long after assignments changed.

Above all, Jeff took great pride in being a father. His children meant the world to him, and he did not take the privilege of being their father lightly. He was devoted to his mother, siblings, adopted children, extended family, and close friends, always making sure the people he loved knew they mattered.

Jeff loved the Lord and was a faithful member of Spring Creek Baptist Church, where he especially enjoyed his Men’s Bible Study and Sunday School class. He spoke openly about his relationship with Jesus and was at peace with the promise of Heaven.

Away from the badge, Jeff enjoyed Conway Twitty and Alan Jackson, keeping his lawn (and sometimes his neighbors’ lawns) mowed, cheering on the Razorbacks with pizza from Larry’s Pizza in Haskell, and spending time at the casinos. He also had a bucket list he was working his way through, and the only thing he didn’t get to cross off was trying out the new Buc-ee’s. Jeff loved him some Buc-ee’s.

Jeff is survived by his children, Morgan Ramsey and J. Alan Ramsey; his mother, Sarah Ramsey; siblings, Rocky (Gina) Ramsey, Robin (Gary) Ramsey Pelton, and Michael (Sherry) Ramsey; adopted children, Sarah, Ashley, and Tim Tate; and many nieces, nephews, cousins, extended family members, and close friends. He will also be deeply missed by his brothers in blue, and by the many people whose lives were touched by him.

He is now reunited in eternity with his father, Bill Ramsey; and grandparents, C.R. and Lottie Bell Statler and James and Willie Mae Ramsey.

Visitation will be held from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. Thursday, August 13, 2026, at Smith Benton Funeral Home, 322 N. Market St., Benton. Funeral services will be held at 10:00 a.m. Friday, August 14, 2026, at Spring Creek Baptist Church, 19200 I-30 Frontage Rd., Benton. Burial will follow at Mt. Harmony Cemetery.

Pallbearers are J. Alan Ramsey, Gary Adams, Ryan Jacks, Greg Church, Tyler Hamilton, and Evan Williams. Honorary pallbearers are Will Bearden, Michael Ramsey, Rocky Ramsey, and Brandon Blaylock.

In lieu of flowers, memorials may be made to CARTI, the Arkansas State Police Foundation, or Spring Creek Baptist Church.

The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to the doctors, nurses, and staff who cared for Jeff, especially the ECMO team at UAMS. Their skill, compassion, and dedication throughout his care will never be forgotten.

Jeff’s watch may have ended on August 7th, but the impact on the lives he touched and the example he left behind will remain.

John Wayne Allen, Jr.

John Wayne Allen, Jr., 47, passed away August 3, 2026. He was born February 6, 1979, in Leavenworth, Kansas, where he grew up before making his way to Hot Springs, Arkansas, in 2014—“all because two people fell in love.”

John was a graduate of the Food Jobs Work Culinary School and found a career that perfectly suited one of his greatest passions. He worked as a chef at Pleasant Valley Country Club in Little Rock, Arkansas. For John, cooking was much more than a job it was his love language. Preparing food was one of the ways he cared for people and showed them what they meant to him.

Above all John adored his daughter and treasured the people he called family. He had a big personality and a style all his own. He loved cars, liked his clothes and shoes to match, and enjoyed both making money and spending it. Those who knew him well will undoubtedly smile remembering one of his favorite responses: “You’re broke.”

John was also known for the sayings that became uniquely his. “Love you to the moon and back until the cows come home” was one of the ways he expressed just how deeply he cared. And those closest to him will surely remember hearing another unmistakably John phrase: “love you Tits.” They were words, jokes, and expressions that became part of the language of loving John and memories his family will carry with them.

John enjoyed watching Real Steel, his favorite movie, and was a fan of Andrew Tate. Whether he was cooking, talking about cars, putting together the perfect outfit, joking with someone he loved, or finding another way to make or spend a dollar. John lived life with a personality that was unmistakably his own.

John was preceded in death by his father, John Wayne Allen, Sr. and his stepson Quinton Ross.

He leaves behind to cherish his memory his life partner of more than 17 years, Melissa Lumley; children, Shelby Allen, Brandon King, Emily Allen, and Chandler Allen; siblings, Jennifer Allen, Carol Goodman, and two adopted sisters; stepmother, Dianna Allen; and a host of extended family members and friends who loved John and will miss him always.

John’s family will hold a private memorial service.

John’s children are asked to contact Smith-Benton Funeral Home at 501-778-7100 as soon as possible.

John will be remembered for his humor, his cooking, his love of cars, his unmistakable sense of style, and most of all, for the love he had for the people who mattered most to him. His was a personality that could never quite be duplicated, and those who loved him will carry his sayings, his laughter, and his memory with them to the moon and back, until the cows come home. Words, jokes, and expressions that became part of the language of loving John and memories his family will carry with them.

Steven Bruce Gregory

Steven Bruce Gregory, 96, of Benton, Arkansas, peacefully passed away on June 17, 2026. He was born in Mountainburg, Arkansas, on July 3, 1929, to Clarence and Betty Gregory. Steven lived a life defined by kindness, humility, and service to others, leaving a lasting impact on everyone fortunate enough to know him. His unwavering dedication to his community, coupled with his warm and welcoming spirit, created a legacy that will continue to be felt for years to come.

For more than a decade, visitors walking through the front doors of Saline Health System were greeted by the same familiar voice — warm, talkative and always ready with directions or a story. For children, there was often an added bonus: a teddy bear delivered with the enthusiasm of someone who never tired of giving them away.

That voice belonged to Steven Gregory, affectionately known throughout the hospital as “Mr. Steven,” a longtime volunteer. Gregory died Wednesday, leaving behind countless memories for the patients, visitors and staff whose lives he touched.

“For many people, Mr. Steven was part of the hospital experience,” said David Gibson, cardiopulmonary director. “Whether you were coming for an appointment, visiting a loved one or reporting for work, there was comfort in seeing him at the front desk. He made a large hospital feel a little more personal.”

Gregory began volunteering in 2005 and went on to serve 8,912 hours — a number he tracked with meticulous care. He followed rules the way some people follow recipes, with precision and pride. Logging his hours wasn’t just a requirement; it reflected how seriously he took his commitment to the hospital and the people who walked through its doors.

Over the years, he held various roles, like delivering checks to team members, assisting with customer service training and serving in the surgery waiting room. But the front desk became his place — where he found purpose, routine and endless opportunities for conversation.

Of all the routines he kept, the one that mattered most to him involved the small bears volunteers stitched by hand. He checked the drawer often, making sure it was full and ready for the next child who needed a distraction or a smile.

“He often told me, ‘I love what I do; I wouldn’t be here if I didn’t,’ and anyone who knew him could see those words were genuine,” said Teresa Sander, volunteer coordinator. “He will be remembered not only for the many hours he gave in volunteer service, but for the kindness, joy and friendship he shared. He loved being here, and we loved having him here.”

To honor Gregory’s many years of service and lasting impact on the hospital community, the hospital installed and dedicated a bench in his honor in their courtyard on Friday, July 3, which would have been Gregory’s 97th birthday.

“Mr. Steven gave our hospital something you can’t measure in hours alone,” said Char Boulch, CEO of Saline Health System. “He made people feel welcomed, cared for and never alone when they walked through our doors. His presence shaped this place in ways we will feel for a long time.”

Family and friends are invited to celebrate the extraordinary life of Steven Bruce Gregory on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at Smith Benton Funeral Home, 322 N. Market St., Benton, Arkansas. Visitation will begin at 12:00 p.m., followed by a Celebration of Life service at 1:00 p.m. Those whose lives were touched by Steven’s kindness, generosity, and unwavering servant’s heart are encouraged to attend as they gather to honor a man who made the world a little brighter, one smile at a time.

item.title: Convicted Saline County double-murderer Timothy Wallace seeks executive clemency from Arkansas governor
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Timothy Wallace, a Saline County man convicted in 2007 of the double murder of his ex-wife and her acquaintance, is seeking executive clemency from the Governor of Arkansas. State authorities are currently accepting public feedback on the application ahead of a scheduled review by the Arkansas Parole Board. Read more below. The application for Executive […]
item.content:encoded:
Timothy Wallace, a Saline County man convicted in 2007 of the double murder of his ex-wife and her acquaintance, is seeking executive clemency from the Governor of Arkansas. State authorities are currently accepting public feedback on the application ahead of a scheduled review by the Arkansas Parole Board. Read more below.




The application for Executive Clemency Commutation filed by Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107, was formally published in a legal notice in accordance with Arkansas state law. His petition will undergo a formal review by the Arkansas Parole Board during the month of October 2026.

Members of the public who wish to comment or express their opinions on Wallace’s application for executive clemency may write to Institutional Release Services, 2801 South Olive Street, Suite 6D, Pine Bluff, Arkansas 71603. To be considered in the review process, all written correspondence must be received prior to August 22, 2026.

The case dates back to the early morning hours of June 26, 2005, when Wallace was age 38. According to court records, Wallace placed a call himself to 911 at approximately 2:30 a.m. indicating that he had shot his former wife, Brandy Wallace, and her male acquaintance, Billy Hassel, at the home the couple had previously shared.

Wallace had surrendered the home to Brandy in an uncontested divorce decree filed just nine days prior to the incident. During the 911 call, which lasted for several hours, Wallace repeatedly threatened suicide and refused to disclose his whereabouts. Saline County sheriff’s deputies eventually located and apprehended him inside his parked pickup truck in a rural section of the county.

At trial, Wallace claimed that he had returned to the home to retrieve personal belongings and shot Hassel in self-defense, asserting that Brandy’s death was accidental. However, forensic evidence presented by the state medical examiner showed that Brandy was shot multiple times at close range while holding her car keys and her cellular phone, while Hassel suffered three gunshot wounds—including shots originating from behind—and severe blunt force trauma consistent with being struck by the butt of a gun.

On June 14, 2007, a Saline County Circuit Court jury convicted Wallace of two counts of capital murder. He was subsequently sentenced on June 18, 2007, to two consecutive terms of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. At this point, 21 years have passed.

Wallace filed several subsequent appeals, arguing various points of trial error, ineffective assistance of counsel, and actual innocence, all of which were subsequently denied or dismissed by the Arkansas Supreme Court and the federal district court.

Having exhausted all standard legal appeals, executive clemency represents his final remaining option for sentence commutation.

FULL LEGAL NOTICE IS AS FOLLOWS:

The notice of application for Executive Clemency of Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 is hereby published as required by Arkansas Code Ann. §5-4-607. Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 was convicted in Saline County, Arkansas on June 14, 2007 of Capital Murder. His information will be reviewed before the Arkansas Parole Board during the month of October , 2026. Wallace, Timothy ADC#139107 is requesting that the Governor of Arkansas grant him Executive Clemency Commutation. Individuals wishing to comment or express their opinions on this application for Executive Clemency may write to Institutional Release Services, 2801 South Olive Street, Suite 6D, Pine Bluff, Arkansas 71603, prior to August 22, 2026.

William Ray Salyers

William Ray Salyers, 78, of Benton, Arkansas, passed away peacefully on July 30, 2026. William was born on January 17, 1948 in War, West Virginia to Arvil and Virgie Salyers. He was a father, grandfather, and brother, and will be missed by all who knew and loved him.

William is survived by two siblings, Calvin Salyers and Stacey Jo Gibson; four children, William Bruce Salyers, Melissa Sue (Shawn) Hill, Karen (James) Kinsey, and Brody Layne Hill, 10 grandchildren, Jessica McDonald, Sidney Salyers, Isabel Salyers, Gavin Hill, Garrett Hill, Blake Photisane, Kenneth Fenimore, Jonathan Fenimore, Steven Kinsey and Savanah Kinsey as well as 20 great grandchildren.

He was preceded in death by his Father Arvil Salyers, his Mother Virgie Salyers, and a sister, Della May Salyers.

A graveside service to celebrate William’s life will be held on Friday, August 7, 2026 at 8:00am at New Rosemont Cemetery in Benton, Arkansas.

 

Marilyn Yvonne Troutt Bagby

Marilyn Yvonne Troutt Bagby, 82, passed into the arms of Jesus at her home on August 1, 2026. She was born on April 3, 1944 in Sheridan to John Loren and Louella Troutt.

In high school, Marilyn worked a weekend job at TG&Y in Little Rock. A coworker introduced her to the love of her life, Johnny. Marilyn graduated from Bryant High School in 1962. She and John married October 6, 1962. They worked hard together and built the home that they always dreamed of providing for their family. Together they had one son, Gordon, and one daughter, Julie. Marilyn was a talented seamstress and spent many hours in her sewing room. She adored her two grandchildren and spent approximately 1,092 Tuesdays over the course of 21 years taking them to the mall for Auntie Ann’s pretzels. She prayed over her loved ones every day during her walk, enjoying her Creator’s beauty and thanking Him for her many blessings. She worked at H&R Block, in investments and for a CPA for many years prior to helping daughter Julie at Bryant Bethel Physical Therapy, PA. There she was the smiling face at the front door, secretary, scheduler, chatter, bookkeeper and grandkid shuttle. John and Marilyn found a new hobby in ballroom dancing in their 70s and could frequently be found cutting a rug at the Senior Center.

Marilyn was an active member at First Southern Baptist Church in Bryant. It was her joy to teach the 2 year old Sunday school class for over 20 years. She poured the love of Jesus into each child that entered her classroom. She enjoyed singing in the choir as long as she was physically able. She has undoubtedly found her voice again and is praising her savior and creator in Heaven.

Martha Jeanette Loomis

Martha Jeanette Loomis, 83, of Prescott, Arkansas, went to be with the Lord on Friday, July 31, 2026, at home, surrounded by the family who adored her. 

Martha was born in Prescott on February 25, 1943, to Fred and Thelma (Haynie) Bolls. She was the fourth of eight children. 

In 1961, Martha married Bill Loomis. They celebrated their sixty-fifth wedding anniversary on June 30. Daughter Melissa was born in 1966, and Mandi joined the family in 1971. 

Martha spent her professional life keeping other people organized. She served as church secretary at First Southern Baptist Church in Bryant, Pastor’s Secretary at Indian Springs Baptist Church, and Office Manager for Econocom and American Computer Solutions, Inc. 

The work closest to her heart was done through her church. For more than forty years, Martha taught the 3-year-old Sunday School class, worked in church nurseries, and helped with Vacation Bible School. She and Bill always kept a watchful eye on their girls from the choir loft. She also maintained a birthday-card ministry for years, sending hundreds of cards and making sure people knew they were remembered. 

Her family dubbed her “The Perfect Sister” because her house was spotless, her flower beds were beautiful, and she gave wonderful parties with fancy serving dishes and decorations. She directed weddings, organized countless church showers, sewed beautiful clothes for herself and her daughters, and made equally fashionable outfits for their Barbies. She was an excellent cook, especially known for her potato salad, and she wore lipstick and jewelry every day, even to mow the lawn. 

Martha and Bill loved being with people. They played cards and dominoes with friends, enjoyed lots of travel over the years, and often had more social plans in a week than their daughters did. They were fun, relaxed, and always ready to enjoy good company. 

Martha lived with Parkinson’s disease for ten years, and Bill never left her side. Even when she could no longer walk or feed herself, she never complained. Not even once.

 Over and over, the people remembering Martha have used the same words: an amazing example of a godly woman. She was that example as a wife, mother, grandmother, sister, aunt, teacher, and friend. She quietly took care of people all her life, never seeking attention or praise. 

She was preceded in death by her parents, Fred and Thelma (Haynie) Bolls, and her brothers, Jack Bolls, Charles Bolls, and Thomas “Buddy” Bolls. 

Left to cherish her memory are her husband, Bill Loomis; her daughters, Melissa Nesbitt and husband Matt, and Mandi Loomis; her grandchildren, Mason and Maya Nesbitt; her sisters, Mary Nell Rogers and husband Jerry, Barbara LaMastus, Dinah Rouse and husband Bob, and Debbie Bolls Whitlock; and her sisters-in-law, Sue Bolls and Kat Bolls. She is also survived by more than 100 nieces and nephews across four generations. 

A celebration of Martha’s life will be held Friday, August 7, 2026, at 1 p.m. at The Hill Barn in Bryant, Arkansas, with Brother Benny Grant officiating. A reception will follow immediately in the same space. Memorial markers will be placed at DeAnn Cemetery in Prescott. In lieu of flowers, memorials may be made in Martha’s memory to The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research: https://tribute.michaeljfox.org/tribute-page.php?id=3646&np=true
